title: DAWN: Accelerating Point Cloud Object Detection via Object-Aware Partitioning and 3D Similarity-Based Filtering
problem: Point cloud object detection for autonomous driving and robotics faces high computational cost due to complex point processing on large per-frame point sets.
motivation: 3D point cloud detection is computationally intensive, limiting real-time deployment in latency-sensitive autonomous systems; opportunity exists to exploit temporal redundancy across frames.
method: DAWN identifies frame-to-frame similarities and filters redundant points through object-aware partitioning based on previous detection results. Axis-sorted point selection refines partitioning for non-uniform point distributions. Efficient 3D similarity algorithm performs point filtering. Flexible latency-accuracy tradeoffs via configurable filtering ratios.
key_novelty: Object-aware partitioning that leverages detection context to enable frame-based similarity filtering and redundancy elimination.
contributions: Object-aware partitioning strategy for localized inter-frame similarity analysis
Axis-sorted point selection for non-uniform point cloud refinement
3D similarity filtering algorithm eliminating 50% of points with negligible accuracy loss
limitations: Acceleration primarily through point filtering; scope limited to autonomous driving/robotics detection; effectiveness on other 3D vision tasks not evaluated.
primary_theme: Frame-based point filtering for efficient 3D detection
